evidence.exact_span: 'In a civil case there must either be the consent of the parties or an acquiescence on their part from which the strong inference is consent.
'Save in the most exceptional circumstances, the trial judge should not himself call a person to give evidence.

However, in a case like the present, I am of opinion that it was not appropriate for his Honour to have used Ms Frank's affidavit in any way, although the parts of the affidavit which his Honour used were simply confirmatory of what the appellant herself had accepted in her cross-examination and also of what the objective evidence revealed.
